leakage_review.reason: Ananya's review: glare_synth.py's black-lift adds a deterministic per-frame floor, so every glared frame's darkest pixel sat at 31-121 vs 0-2 for every clean frame -- zero overlap across all 298 held-out frames, confirmed directly against this repo's data. min_pixel > 2 alone was a 100%-accurate classifier; it reflects a real physical effect (veiling glare does lift black level) made artificially deterministic by the synthesis, not real generalizable signal.
leakage_review.sanity_check_after_removal: accuracy stayed ~100% (MLP: 100%, plain logistic regression: 99.66%, 1 error). Checked this is NOT a second hidden leak: logistic regression coefficients have no single dominant weight, and every remaining feature has genuine class-range overlap on this data (verified per-feature) -- consistent with legitimate combined signal (mean brightness + contrast + chromatic shift + upper-region brightness), not another shortcut.
leakage_review.open_caveat: this validation set is still synthetic and deterministic (four fixed glare recipes, no sensor noise), so near-100% here does not guarantee the same held up against real glare photos (CLAUDE.md section 13, the GLARE dataset). Retraining once glare_synth.py adds sensor noise / floor jitter (Ananya's proposed fix) would give a more trustworthy number.
